A spoken 言 tongue 舌; 舌 also provides the pronunciation
Phonosemantic compound. 言 represents the meaning and 舌 represents the sound.
合會善言也。从言𠯑聲。《傳》曰：“告之話言。”

Phono-semantic compound (形聲 /形声, OC *ɡroːds): semantic 言 (“word”) + phonetic 𠯑 (OC *ɡroːd). The right component is not related to 舌 (OC *ɦbljed, “tongue”).
Cognate with 曰 (OC *ɢʷad) according to Sagart (1999); if so, it is from Proto-Sino-Tibetan *grwas (“to speak; word”), whence Tibetan གྲོས་སྡུར་བྱེད་པ (gros sdur byed pa, “to consult; to discuss”) (STEDT).

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 說明 / 說文釋形; 字樣說明
evidence.text: The dictionary says 話 is explained in Shuowen as “合會善言也。从言，𠯑聲” and records a Zhou-script form 譮 “从會.” It warns that the right side is easily mistaken for 舌 because of the meaning ‘speaking,’ but identifies it as 𠯑, a phonetic element, rather than 舌 used ideographically. This supports 言 as semantic and 𠯑 as phonetic; it does not establish that 𠯑 depicts a particular object.
evidence.title: [A03824] 話 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.field: 《說文》; 形義通解; 中古音
evidence.text: The entry gives the Shuowen analysis “合會善言也。从言，𠯑聲” and analyzes 話 as 言 plus phonetic 𠯑. It reports the poem 《詩·大雅·抑》 “慎爾出話” with 毛傳 glossing 話 as 善言 (‘good words’). It also gives later examples: Yuan Zhen’s Tang poem for 話 as listening to a narrated story, a Tang Meng Haoran poem for ‘talk/discuss,’ and 《書·盤庚中》 for ‘inform/tell’ according to Ma Rong’s gloss as quoted by Lu Deming. These attest lexical uses in texts, but do not alone supply a secure dated sequence of semantic changes. The entry records 話’s Guangyun fanqie 下快 and Middle Chinese categories 匣母, 去聲, 蟹攝, 夬韻, 合口二等.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 話
